observations.summary: governance requires a non-persistable empty transfer inbox directory
observations.expected: A valid external workspace must survive clone/checkout with governance-valid transfer state. Empty runtime directories must be deterministically materialized by a supported Kit lifecycle command, represented by a persistable Kit-owned carrier, or treated as a legitimate absent/empty state.
observations.observed: workspace init source owns creation of .agentic/transfer/inbox, while governance check requires the directory itself. The current repository has no inbox directory. observations.impact: A valid external workspace can fail governance after checkout solely because an empty runtime carrier directory is absent, blocking governed lifecycle work and encouraging agents to fabricate Kit-owned state.

observations.repair: Close the external-workspace lifecycle across checkout: provide deterministic Kit provisioning/persistable carrier semantics, or make governance resolve inbox absence through the same legitimate empty-state model as transfer state. Expose exact remediation through a high-level Kit command.
observations.regression: Fresh external workspace init -> commit/push -> fresh clone/checkout -> governance check must pass without manually creating .agentic/transfer/inbox; no pending transfer command must remain a deterministic NO_COMMAND state.

families.title: Workspace lifecycle bootstrap is not closed after successful external workspace init
families.expected: dpa-intake/workspace init must either preflight lifecycle metadata, normalize it canonically, or return a deterministic remediation path before doctor is expected to pass.
families.observed: workspace init reported PASS and agentic-kit check passed, but doctor failed iteratively on missing/invalid Status, Decision status, and Review policy metadata.
families.impact: Fresh external-workspace bootstrap reports success before the lifecycle contract is actually closed; the operator must reverse-engineer document metadata iteratively.
families.workaround: Add the lifecycle headers manually according to the installed Kit contract.
families.repair: Integrate lifecycle preflight/remediation into dpa-intake/workspace init, or provide a canonical lifecycle-normalization command.
families.regression: Fresh external repo with planning docs lacking lifecycle metadata must either block before init, pass doctor after init, or emit one deterministic remediation command.

families.title: Planning-document slice gate leaks Kit self-hosting assumptions into external workspaces
families.expected: External-manifest workspace slice gates must resolve only workspace-applicable gates, project-native tests, and explicitly registered extra gates.
families.observed: slice gate --kind planning-doc attempted Kit self-hosting test paths and Kit documentation-mesh requirements absent from the external repository.
families.impact: Healthy external workspaces are classified as broken because they do not contain the Kit repository's own source/tests/docs structure.
families.workaround: Use external-workspace-safe project tests plus agentic-kit check/doctor instead of the affected higher-level gate.
families.repair: Centralize workspace-mode/capability resolution and make slice gates profile-aware.
families.regression: A minimal external manifest workspace without Kit source files must not fail planning-doc gate because Kit self-hosting paths are absent.

families.title: Handoff-state paths and fresh bootstrap state are inconsistent
families.expected: Exactly one authoritative handoff-state resolver/path per workspace mode, with an explicit legitimate fresh/no-previous-handoff state.
families.observed: Commands referenced .agentic/handoff_state.yaml, .agentic/state/handoff/handoff_state.yaml, and directory-level state differently; fresh workspace checks could raise FileNotFoundError.
families.impact: A newly initialized workspace cannot rely on a single deterministic handoff authority and read-only handoff checks may fail on a legitimate empty state.
families.workaround: Use the specific currently functioning transfer/handoff surfaces and avoid inventing missing state files.
families.repair: Centralize handoff path resolution and model NO_PREVIOUS_HANDOFF explicitly.
families.regression: Immediately after workspace init, handoff check, post-merge-check and work recover must classify deterministically without traceback.

families.title: governance check is not external-workspace aware
families.expected: governance check must resolve the same external-manifest workspace mode as doctor.

families.workaround: Treat doctor/check as authoritative external-workspace baseline until governance check is corrected.

families.title: Tracked successor handoff projections are self-stale after their own commit
families.expected: A deterministic successor handoff must converge on a trustworthy final repository identity without requiring perpetual re-render/commit cycles.
families.observed: chat-switch-complete generated tracked files containing current HEAD; committing those files created a new HEAD that none of them referenced; rerendering dirtied the same files again. Later Phase-5 closeout reproduction showed five Kit-generated tracked successor projections surviving post-merge closeout: restore-known-volatile did not recognize them, normalize-session blocked the next work start as dirty_worktree, and post-merge-settle --after-pr 22 rejected the same files as dirty_product_paths_before_post_merge_complete.
families.impact: The Kit cannot simultaneously guarantee committed successor package, exact final-HEAD identity, and clean tracked worktree with the current projection model. The defect can make the next high-level work cycle unreachable through supported settlement commands.
families.workaround: Render final-HEAD successor projections after the final code/remote HEAD is fixed and keep those exact-final-HEAD projections volatile/uncommitted. For already affected workspaces, after preserving evidence and exhausting supported settlement paths, restore only the exact known generated successor-projection paths to the committed state as a bounded recovery exception.
families.repair: Decouple durable committed handoff source from volatile exact-final-HEAD projection, or introduce a transaction/identity model that explicitly understands the handoff commit boundary.
families.regression: A disposable clone must prove that final successor authority remains exact and validation-clean without a self-staling render->commit->rerender loop.

families.title: External-workspace governance does not detect stale or ambiguous continuation authority
families.expected: External-workspace governance should validate freshness and consistency of active continuation authority and clearly distinguish product-owned canonical sources, Kit operating state, registries, and generated projections.

families.impact: A successor LLM can receive obsolete or ambiguous direction despite a formally green lifecycle.
families.workaround: Define explicit Cockpit-side document authority and canonical values until the Kit provides this governance.
families.repair: Add external-workspace authority checks for stale active phase/status, registry coverage/intent, and contradictions between open_tasks_source and the selected workspace/project-direction model.
families.regression: An external workspace with stale active status, empty/unclassified registry, or contradictory successor authority must warn or fail deterministically.

families.title: Canonical document facts are not propagated across registered documents
families.expected: A project should be able to declare a canonical fact once and have Kit-managed/generated documents reference or refresh it deterministically; project-owned prose should be audited for stale/conflicting values and only rewritten when explicitly opted in.
families.observed: The Kit can register and lifecycle-check documents, but there is no declared single-source mechanism for shared project facts such as one desired DOI link, concept DOI, project URL, or release version, nor deterministic detection/refresh of stale occurrences across documents.
families.impact: Shared metadata can drift across otherwise valid documents, leaving contradictory DOI links, versions, URLs, or other facts while document lifecycle checks remain green.
families.workaround: Define explicit Cockpit-side document authority and canonical values until the Kit provides this governance.
families.repair: Extend the documentation registry with canonical facts/metadata and reference declarations; add drift audit plus safe normalization for explicitly managed/generated surfaces, and review-required findings for project-owned prose.
families.regression: Declare one canonical DOI link, place an old conflicting DOI in registered managed/generated and project-owned documents, then require deterministic managed refresh plus a review finding for non-opted-in project prose.

families.title: High-level external-workspace workflows should support contract-first guided execution
families.expected: A mutating high-level workflow should expose a machine-readable contract-first plan that detects repository context, proposes explicit changed paths, reports missing decisions and blockers, and yields an execution-ready plan before mutation.
families.observed: During Cockpit foreign-repository closeout, work finish required branch, title, message and explicit repeated path selection. The Kit behaved correctly once fully specified, but the calling agent discovered parts of the invocation contract incrementally. An explicit-path dry-run then returned blockers=[], result_status=PASS and a coherent merge/post-merge plan.
families.impact: Agents can waste iterations reimplementing or guessing Kit orchestration contracts even when the underlying high-level workflow is sound.
families.workaround: Inspect --help and run a non-mutating JSON dry-run with explicit paths before --execute.
families.repair: Standardize Inspect -> Plan -> Validate -> Execute -> Verify for mutating high-level commands; make dry-run JSON surface detected context, proposed paths, required inputs, blockers and an execution-ready invocation or equivalent structured contract.
families.regression: In an external workspace with multiple dirty paths, a first contract/planning call should deterministically identify or propose all required inputs and paths without mutation, and a subsequent execute using that plan should not require undocumented agent-side inference.

families.title: Merged-work-branch cleanup is not idempotent when the authoritative remote ref is already absent
families.expected: After verified merge, delete-merged-work-branch must adjudicate the desired cleanup postcondition. If the authoritative remote branch is already absent, remote cleanup is already satisfied and the wrapper must return deterministic PASS/NOOP or an equivalent successful idempotent state.
families.observed: During Phase-8 final housekeeping, delete-merged-work-branch successfully verified the PR as MERGED, then attempted `git push origin --delete feature/phase8-automated-multi-round-bridge`. Git reported `remote ref does not exist`; the wrapper returned BLOCKED with blocker `remote_delete_failed`. Step 335R1 independently proved that the authoritative remote ref was already absent and only stale local remote-tracking state had made cleanup appear necessary.
families.impact: Automated lifecycle/housekeeping can block despite the desired end state already being achieved, forcing agents to diagnose a false mutation failure when no repair mutation is required.
families.workaround: Adjudicate authoritative remote state read-only before retrying cleanup; when authoritative absence is proven, do not repeat the delete mutation. Prune stale local tracking state only when separately justified.

families.title: No recovery route for main with local changes or local commits
families.expected: A Kit route recovers main without losing work when it carries uncommitted changes or commits that are not on origin/main: it saves them on a new rescue branch, realigns main with origin/main only after verifying that the rescue branch contains everything, and reports the result as JSON; destructive variants keep the dry-run signature pattern of work discard-changes.
families.observed: Kit 1.0.13 in a sandbox clone of agp-Cockpit main ad2a38d (2026-10-02): `transfer branch-create rescue/t1 --start-point HEAD` with a dirty main fails ('Clean or preserve local changes before creating a branch.'); `work discard-changes` is BLOCKED on main (blocker main-branch, by design); `transfer sync-main` with main one commit ahead of origin/main fails (blockers: normalize-session_failed); `work recover` restores only known volatile files and states it 'never runs reset, clean, checkout, or broad restore over product files'. Covered: main behind origin/main (`transfer sync-main` PASS), detached HEAD (`transfer branch-switch main` PASS), discarding changes on a work branch (`work discard-changes`, dry-run signature, then --execute). The Kit's own work-order validator forbids `git reset --hard` in work orders, so a remote work order cannot fill the gap either.
families.impact: The Cockpit's full Wiederherstellen (P8) has no Kit route for two of the most common disturbances; filling the gap would need raw git outside the Kit (Cockpit-local or in a work order), which breaks the architecture principle that the Kit controls every repository change.
families.workaround: Owner's decision 2026-10-02: the full Wiederherstellen button waits for this fix; the basic Wiederherstellen (diagnosis through the remote LLM, Kit routes only) stays, and a disturbance without a Kit route ends in NEEDS_HUMAN for the owner to resolve by hand.
families.repair: Add a non-lossy rescue route (for example `work rescue --json`): dirty main → new rescue branch carrying the changes; main ahead/diverged → rescue branch at HEAD, then main reset to origin/main after a containment check; detached HEAD with unique commits → rescue branch first. Dry-run by default with a signature, --execute with --expected-signature, never a remote effect.
families.regression: In a clone: dirty main and main one commit ahead each end with main == origin/main, a clean worktree and a rescue branch that contains every change or commit; repeated runs are idempotent.

families.title: Communication refresh on a work branch blocks the lifecycle that would publish it
families.expected: A branch that changes a rule source (here .agentic/config.yaml) can be finished: the rule acknowledgement is refreshed locally and the communication-rule capsule travels with the branch's own pull request; nothing requires the capsule on main before that pull request can be created.
families.observed: Kit 1.0.14 in agp-Cockpit, branch chore/kit-1.0.15 adding `publication: none` to .agentic/config.yaml (a rule source): (1) pr-create-complete BLOCKED with snapshot_id_mismatch three times although `rules acknowledge` succeeded before each run — the workspace tracked .agentic/rule_ack/current.json and the pre-push volatile restore put the stale committed copy back (Cockpit-side cause, fixed by untracking); (2) the remote side then ran `rules communication-refresh --publish`, which wrote .agentic/rule_ack/communication_refresh_pending.json with blocks_normal_go=true and remote_ref=main ('Send d2 only after the rule capsule is committed and remote-readable'); pr-create-complete then BLOCKED with 'Commit and publish the rule capsule before sending d2' (reproduced in a sandbox) — a deadlock, because only that pull request could put the capsule on main; push-current was correctly refused by the Cockpit in a standard task.
families.impact: A finishing run cannot complete once the communication refresh was started; recovery needs a human to move the pending file away.
families.workaround: Stop the run; move .agentic/rule_ack/communication_refresh_pending.json and the generated capsule files out of the way (kept under .agentic/tmp/stale-1656/); untrack .agentic/rule_ack/; rerun Abschließen.
families.repair: Let the capsule be published by the branch's own pull request (pending state scoped to the branch, satisfied by the PR head), or keep the pending state advisory for pr-create-complete; document which rule sources trigger a communication refresh.
families.regression: A branch that changes .agentic/config.yaml finishes with pr-create-complete --post-merge-complete after rules acknowledge, with or without a preceding communication-refresh --publish.
evidence: sandbox: pr-create-complete BLOCK 'Commit and publish the rule capsule before sending d2' with the pending file present; PASSES the rule gate without it after untracking .agentic/rule_ack/current.json

workflow_lessons.title: Evidence-first convergence workflow reduces patch instability and false-positive repairs
workflow_lessons.finding: Delay product mutation until bounded inventory, ownership/call-path seam mapping, and contextual adjudication demonstrate a concrete competing authority, invariant violation, or failing behavior.
recommended_sequence: smallest justified mutation only when evidence requires it
broader integration/governance gates at controlled boundaries

workflow_lessons.title: Preserve Kit-owned multi-stage lifecycle and prefer high-level closeout wrappers
workflow_lessons.finding: During PR #2 validation, low-level transfer commands were manually composed after `work finish --execute --no-merge`, bypassing the Kit's higher-level multi-stage closeout abstraction.
workflow_lessons.lesson: Exercise the highest-level supported Kit wrapper for the intended lifecycle before treating failures of internal/low-level subcommands as Kit defects; use low-level commands only for diagnosis after the wrapper path is observed or shown unavailable.
required_validation_sequence: execute the high-level wrapper under observation
only then inspect an internal low-level step if the wrapper fails
preserve partial state as evidence and avoid manual fallback
classify a Kit defect against the intended wrapper contract

workflow_lessons.finding: When repeated patch failures expose successive coupled assertions or symptoms in the same failure domain, stop local micro-patching and perform a bounded read-only Megablick over the complete lifecycle, invariants, call path, persistence, tests, and authority boundaries before the next mutation.
workflow_lessons.lesson: Treat the failure domain as a system: distinguish product defect from stale test model, map coupled expectations and delivered-path wiring, then make one coherent justified repair and validate broadly. A third blind mutation in the same family is forbidden.
evidence: Steps 592R9-592R14: fail-fast exposed a coupled six-to-seven-action fixture drift; bounded diagnosis identified the shared model and enabled one coherent correction.

workflow_lessons.finding: LLM repository work must be fail-closed behind existing Agentic Project Kit command-authority and workflow gates; guessed Kit CLI, raw lifecycle reconstruction, and bypass of missing authority surfaces defeat the Kit's purpose.
workflow_lessons.lesson: Use the installed command manifest, agentic-kit command-for, audit-command-authority, instruction lint, rules validate-sources, rule-registry/workflow-guard, workspace orchestrators, and work finish as mandatory enforcement. Do not invent a parallel governance mechanism.
evidence: Steps 597-601R2: repeated LLM-side command assumptions were blocked; 601R2 proved packaged audit-command-authority fails closed on missing authority surfaces.

workflow_lessons.finding: LLM repository work becomes unreliable when command syntax, source shape, policy files, or workflow prerequisites are inferred instead of established from repository and installed-Kit authority.
workflow_lessons.lesson: Before mutation, establish exact command authority with the installed manifest and agentic-kit command-for, and establish exact source/schema shape from the repository. If authority is missing or contradictory, fail closed and diagnose; never fabricate Kit-owned state or reconstruct a mapped raw Git/GitHub workflow.
workflow_lessons.impact: This removes avoidable mutation failures caused by guessed CLI contracts, guessed JSON structures, and guessed policy prerequisites.

workflow_lessons.finding: A mandatory workflow guard currently dereferences .agentic/rule_preservation.yaml unconditionally even though this external workspace neither tracks nor historically contained that file.
workflow_lessons.lesson: A fail-closed guard must distinguish a policy violation from absent or non-applicable adoption prerequisite state. Missing prerequisite authority must produce a bounded actionable diagnostic, not an unhandled traceback; the caller must not synthesize the missing policy file.
workflow_lessons.impact: External-workspace governance remains strict without forcing agents to invent Kit-owned policy state.
preferred_kit_solution: Resolve workspace applicability first. If rule preservation is not applicable to the current external workspace, return NOT_APPLICABLE or SKIP_WITH_REASON instead of treating the missing file as an error.

If rule preservation is applicable, the Kit must own deterministic bootstrap during workspace init/adopt/upgrade from authoritative rule registry/capsules and generate the canonical preservation file itself.

If required preservation semantics cannot be derived deterministically, block with a bounded machine-readable remediation plan that names the missing decisions; require user review/approval of semantics rather than manual file construction.
Never silently bypass an applicable guard and never fabricate preservation semantics.

workflow_lessons.finding: agentic-kit work finish dry-run accepted a path set containing .agentic/rule_ack/current.json, while execute later rejected that same volatile path at commit time.
workflow_lessons.lesson: A lifecycle dry-run must validate the same commit-path admissibility constraints as execute. Volatile runtime paths must be rejected during planning, before any commit/handoff/push side effects occur.
evidence: Step 617 execute blocked at transfer commit
Step 617R1 succeeded past commit only after excluding the volatile path
workflow_lessons.impact: Improves dry-run/execute parity and prevents partially advanced lifecycle state from a plan that was never executable as presented.

workflow_lessons.title: Evidence-backed supersedable operational experience registry
workflow_lessons.finding: Agentic repository work can rediscover previously evidenced failure patterns when operational lessons remain only in chat/history or unstructured execution artifacts.
workflow_lessons.lesson: Maintain an advisory machine-readable experience registry with applicability predicates, exact provenance, revision revalidation, deterministic counterchecks, and explicit supersession. Current repository/task/Kit authority always outranks experience.
